summary.text: Bob Hasegawa is a Washington state senator who was elected to the Senate in 2012 after serving in the state House of Representatives from 2005 to 2012. His official biography describes him as chair of the Senate Democratic Caucus (Majority Caucus) and a member of the Rules, Ways & Means, Business, Economic Development and Trade, and State Government, Elections & Tribal Affairs committees.

paragraphs.text: Hasegawa is a lifelong resident of the 11th Legislative District, according to his official biography.
It says he grew up on Beacon Hill in Seattle and attended Cleveland High School, and that his family was incarcerated during World War II because of their Japanese heritage.
The page describes him as a longtime labor and social justice activist.
His biography says he was a member of the Teamsters Union for 32 years and was the elected leader of Teamsters Local 174 for three terms, nine years.

It says he was a founding member of the Asian Pacific American Labor Alliance (AFL-CIO) and served on the boards of MLK Labor, the Washington State Labor Council and the Japanese American Citizens League-Seattle.

For education, the page lists time at the University of Washington, a master's degree in public administration from the Daniel J. Evans School, an associate's degree from Shoreline Community College and a bachelor's degree from Antioch University Seattle.
The page says Hasegawa was elected to the House of Representatives in 2005, held the seat through 2012, and was then elected to the Senate.
It says he also chairs the Joint Administrative Rules Review Committee and is a member of the Joint Legislative Audit and Review Committee.
